agent_result.summary: A fixed-same-game, multi-model EPISODE study cannot be launched today. The commit-authority substrate (Python<->Godot round trip, in-process budget enforcement, replay/tamper checks) is real and reusable, but the runner's live model surface is hardcoded to the Codex CLI with no Claude/Gemini sibling, and the unit of execution is a one-shot scripted assignment (<=2 model calls vs one frozen fixture case), not a sustained per-model playthrough bounded by episode caps. The development-comparison-20261023 panel (general_rule vs ontology_representation, multi-provider coding-agent candidates) is a separate, PROPOSED_NOT_EXECUTED study and correctly serves only as contrast.

usable_existing_components: Python<->Godot commit-authority round trip: run_godot bootstrap/experiment/reexecution/tamper-rejection sidecars with sha256-verified state refs and byte-preservation checks
In-process GoalController session/budget state machine with all six caps mechanically enforced and independently testable via BudgetExceeded
Frozen-fixture/manifest/replay/provenance pipeline: make_assignments, freeze_manifest, aggregate, replay_report, sha256 manifest generation
One working live model backend (Codex CLI, arm P) with schema-validated typed-intent output and execution-attempt accounting via execution_observer
missing_composition: A Claude and a Gemini proposal path analogous to the Codex one, wired into the actual target runner (new IntentInterpreter branches or new ProposalAdapter subclasses with a verified per-provider subprocess/API contract)
An episode-level driver loop that repeats intent/plan/action cycles toward goal_reached until a budget or time cap fires, replacing today's <=2-call-per-assignment scripted exchange
A model-identity field threaded through the frozen protocol/schema and into assignment/record provenance (currently provenance.model is None for arm P)
A new evaluation/claim-boundary packet scoping what a multi-model episode result may and may not claim, analogous to the existing CLAIM_BOUNDARY discipline
agent_result.unit_of_analysis_mismatch: Existing scripts define the unit as one case x arm x repetition assignment (assignment_count=72 for the screening packet), bounded to at most two model-intent calls against one frozen initial state. A fixed-same-game multi-model EPISODE study requires the unit to be one full playthrough per model against the same game instance, run until goal_reached or a budget/time cap fires, with model identity as an explicit factor. Scaling today's grid across new models would multiply case-rows, not produce episodes; no code aggregates multiple replan/action cycles into one per-model episode record.
agent_result.episode_time_call_caps_mechanically_enfo: Yes in isolation - max_intent_calls, max_replans, max_action_attempts, max_plan_expansions, intent_deadline_ms, and episode_deadline_ms all raise BudgetExceeded and are model-independent; the Godot-side wall-clock timeout is enforced via subprocess.run(timeout=...). No, not yet for an actual episode - no driver loop currently composes repeated intent cycles into one episode bounded by those caps; today they bound a single assignment's <=2-call exchange.
prerequisite_list: Implement and verify a Claude and a Gemini proposal surface wired into the target runner with a provider-specific subprocess/API contract (timeout, schema validation, execution-attempt accounting) equivalent to codex_oauth_llm.py
Add an explicit model-identity field to the frozen protocol/schema and to assignment/record provenance
Design and implement an episode-level driver loop bounded by episode_deadline_ms/max_intent_calls/max_replans, with its own frozen fixture/case contract distinct from or extending validated-v5
Verify Godot binary availability and the live-integration test lane (test_godot_experimental_game.py) in the actual execution environment before any engine-side readiness claim
Freeze a new evaluation/claim-boundary block for the multi-model episode study consistent with this codebase's existing no-superiority/no-efficacy discipline
agent_result.no_claims_of_live_proof: No code was executed, no model or engine binary was invoked, and no test was run as part of this audit; all findings are source-grounded path:line anchors from static inspection only.

interpretation: Existing NPC Godot/Python authority and budget code can be reused, but it is not a composed fixed-game multi-provider full-episode evaluation harness or proof of current live readiness.
hash_capture_method: shasum -a 256 on the ten cited files after the static audit; source drift invalidates subsequent reliance on these anchors. This does not prove engine/provider execution.
